The migrated file is at `out/module.ts`. It bundles to 739 bytes (min+gzip), with 113 bytes of my own code, and type checking shows no errors in it. I couldn't compare either figure with the original, because lodash isn't installed. `src/module.ts` fails to bundle and fails type checking for that reason, and I didn't install anything.

I read the installed es-toolkit (1.53.2) before choosing functions:

- **`publicFields`:** uses `pick` from `es-toolkit/object`. Its declaration takes `(obj, keys[])` and returns `Pick<T, K>`, which matches the original return type.
- **`totalAge`:** uses `sumBy` from `es-toolkit/math`. That version only accepts a function, not the lodash `'age'` string shorthand. So I added the small adapter `(r) => r.age`.
- **`preview`:** uses `truncate` imported as the default export of `es-toolkit/compat/truncate`. The main entry points don't export `truncate`, so the compat version is the only es-toolkit option. I read its source, and it follows lodash's behaviour: same default omission `...` and same handling of `length`. A quick run gave `aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa...` for a 50-character input and returned `short` unchanged. I didn't run a full comparison against the original, since it can't run here.

Importing `truncate` from the `es-toolkit/compat` barrel gave the same 738 bytes as the per-file import (739), which is the figure I kept. No lodash import remains.
